section_summary: This section documents requests, clearances, refusals, and documentary requirements for foreign businesspeople, missionaries, researchers, diplomats, and other travelers seeking entry into occupied Japan and Okinawa. It includes individual applications and military permits, correspondence with foreign embassies, discussion of trader quotas and a liberalized missionary policy, and SCAP directives aimed at suppressing illegal Korean immigration. Major individual case files concern Antonios Karalis, Moses E. Kaptzan, Marcelo Nubla, Frank Lingenco, Manuel Sternberg, Sherif Soubra, and several Philippine nationals.

subfiles.title: Pepsi-Cola request for Antonios Karalis's return to Japan
subfiles.from: R. Van Horn, Pepsi-Cola Company Export Department
subfiles.about: Requests expedited permission for Antonios Karalis to return to his employment and wife in Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Pepsi-Cola describes Karalis's wartime internment and satisfactory employment, requesting prompt permission for his return to Japan.

subfiles.title: Application of Antonios Karalis to enter occupied territory
subfiles.about: Applies for indefinite entry to Japan to resume employment and rejoin his wife.
subfiles.summary: Karalis supplies his identity, wartime history, employment, travel purpose, and proposed contacts in Yokohama.

subfiles.title: State Department request for Karalis's departure details
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Requests Karalis's departure date, port, and transportation before delivery of his military permit.
subfiles.summary: State reports Karalis's clearance and seeks travel details needed to waive his alien exit-permit requirement.

subfiles.title: Referral of Karalis application to the Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Asks the Army to refer Karalis's application to SCAP and report the decision.
subfiles.summary: State forwards Karalis's application for SCAP consideration, noting prior discussion with Captain Rawls.

subfiles.title: Handwritten processing note on Karalis application
subfiles.about: Records an illegible processing annotation associated with the Karalis case.
subfiles.summary: Largely illegible handwritten administrative note.

subfiles.title: Alfred Morgan request for research travel information
subfiles.about: Asks how to obtain permission for a brief research visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Morgan seeks access to Japanese sources needed for his thesis on wartime fiscal policy, citing prospective Harvard support.

subfiles.title: Reply to Alfred Morgan on entry regulations
subfiles.about: Reports that Japan-entry regulations remain unchanged and offers notice of any future change.
subfiles.summary: The Department advises that no regulatory change presently permits Morgan's proposed research trip.

subfiles.title: Confirmation of William K. Clark's clearance
subfiles.from: D. O'Brien, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Records Army confirmation that William K. Clark was cleared to re-enter Japan for twenty-one days.
subfiles.summary: Miss Flickinger confirms Clark's SCAP clearance under Circular 8 and discusses notifying him of the decision.

subfiles.title: Extension of Hussein Touty's stay in Japan
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests notification of Iran that Hussein Touty's authorized stay was extended through December 29.
subfiles.summary: Army headquarters reports Touty's revised departure date and asks State to inform the Iranian Embassy.

subfiles.title: Notification to Iran concerning Hussein Touty
subfiles.about: Informs Iran of Hussein Touty's SCAP clearance and extended authorized stay in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The draft note recounts Touty's permission to enter Japan and reports his extended departure deadline.

subfiles.title: Pakistan request for a business-traveler quota
subfiles.about: Requests an early allocation of places for Pakistani business representatives to visit Japan.
subfiles.summary: Pakistan seeks a share of the foreign-business quota after learning that entry decisions are made in Washington.

subfiles.title: State response on Pakistani business travel to Japan
subfiles.about: Explains procedures for submitting Pakistani business-travel requests to SCAP through the State Department.
subfiles.summary: State outlines Circular 8 procedures and offers its communications facilities until Pakistan has an accredited representative in Japan.

subfiles.title: Travel details for Moses E. Kaptzan
subfiles.about: Records Kaptzan's Mexican travel document and planned Pan American departure from California.
subfiles.summary: James Michelson supplies details needed to waive Kaptzan's exit permit and requests special-delivery dispatch of his military permit.

subfiles.title: Delivery of Kaptzan's military permit
subfiles.about: Encloses Kaptzan's Japan-entry permit and confirms waiver of his United States exit permit.
subfiles.summary: Kaptzan was cleared for a twenty-one-day visit; immigration offices were notified of the exit-permit waiver.

subfiles.title: Commerce application for Moses E. Kaptzan to visit Japan
subfiles.about: Seeks permission for Kaptzan to reestablish Japanese trade connections and develop import-export business.
subfiles.summary: The application describes Kaptzan's firms, prewar fur trade through Nozaki Brothers, intended cities, and proposed commodities. It presents him as an experienced East Asian trader seeking to renew commercial relationships.

subfiles.title: Autobiographical statement of Moses E. Kaptzan
subfiles.about: Describes Kaptzan's residence, family, employment, nationality, and immigration history.
subfiles.summary: Kaptzan recounts his life from Siberia through Japan, China, Shanghai, the United States, and Mexico, emphasizing his trading experience. He explains his former Soviet documentation, current stateless status, Mexican travel document, and pending United States immigration application.

subfiles.title: Hwa Mei update on Kaptzan's Mexican status
subfiles.from: James Michelson, Hwa Mei Trading Corporation
subfiles.to: Office of International Trade, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Reports that Kaptzan surrendered his Soviet certificate and obtained a Mexican stateless-person travel document.
subfiles.summary: Hwa Mei offers a passport copy and urges expedited permission because it wishes to begin business with Japan.

subfiles.title: Waiver of Kaptzan's exit permit
subfiles.about: Records telephonic waiver of Kaptzan's exit permit for trader-quota travel.
subfiles.summary: Exit-permit waiver recorded for Kaptzan's California departure to Japan.

subfiles.title: Notification of William K. Clark's re-entry approval
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP approval for Clark to re-enter Japan on December 27.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is advised that Clark's conditions and documentation follow those stated in an earlier telegram.

subfiles.title: Commerce certification for Edmond Sassoon
subfiles.about: Forwards Commerce approval of Edmond Sassoon under the United States January trader quota.
subfiles.summary: Sassoon's name was submitted to the Army's Military Permit Section.

subfiles.title: Application of Edmond Sassoon to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Edmond Sassoon / A. and I. Hedaya Company
subfiles.about: Lists Sassoon's firm, position, capitalization, and proposed textile and industrial trade.
subfiles.summary: Sassoon applies as a purchasing agent for a firm without prewar Japanese business.

subfiles.title: Effect of missionary-policy change on alien travelers
subfiles.about: Assesses how the proposed SCAP missionary-policy revision affects alien missionary cases.
subfiles.summary: O'Brien concludes that State's permit-delivery work is unchanged but recommends clarifying that alien missionaries remain subject to Circular 8.

subfiles.title: Army transmittal of new missionary policy
subfiles.about: Forwards the new Japan missionary policy and proposes a correction concerning the initiating agency.
subfiles.summary: The policy was to take effect January 2, 1948, with requests initiated through the State Department.

subfiles.title: SCAP liberalization of missionary policy
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Chief, Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Establishes liberalized procedures for admitting missionaries to occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: SCAP delegates blanket clearance for qualified American missionaries endorsed by recognized mission boards while retaining Circular 8 procedures for foreign nationals. Missionaries must avoid burdening the Japanese or occupation forces, arrange non-occupation support and transport, and refrain from commercial activity. The policy also prescribes certification, reporting, and possible revocation.

subfiles.title: SCAP clearance for Victor S. Reuben
subfiles.about: Records clearance of an Iraqi trader in Shanghai to enter Japan in early January.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Simpson reports Reuben's trader-quota clearance; O'Brien agrees to notify the Shanghai consulate.

subfiles.title: Internal notice of Victor S. Reuben's clearance
subfiles.about: Reports Army permission for Reuben to enter Japan during the approved January period.
subfiles.summary: Internal routing memorandum relaying Reuben's Japan-entry clearance.

subfiles.title: Airgram notifying Shanghai of Reuben's clearance
subfiles.about: Notifies the consulate that Reuben may enter Japan between January 1 and 15, 1948.
subfiles.summary: Clearance and documentation are to follow the conditions in an earlier airgram.

subfiles.title: Referral of Iraqi consular-processing proposal
subfiles.about: Refers Iraq's proposal to route Japan-entry applications through British representatives.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Army to obtain SCAP's decision on allowing British consular representatives to present Iraqi cases. Chappell sees no objection and expects the arrangement to reduce administrative work.

subfiles.title: Iraqi request for British handling of Japan-entry applications
subfiles.about: Requests approval for British consulates to transmit Iraqi applications directly to military authorities in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Iraq argues that routing applications through the American Embassy in Baghdad and Washington is unnecessarily slow. It proposes using existing British consular arrangements where Iraq has no offices.

subfiles.title: Entry inquiry for Kinachi Kasado
subfiles.about: Provides identity and itinerary details for Kinachi Kasado's proposed commercial visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kasado seeks six to nine months in Japan to develop French-Japanese import and export relations.

subfiles.title: Application of Joseph Ingster to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph Ingster / American Dutch Wools, Inc.
subfiles.to: Office of International Trade, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Seeks permission for Ingster to conduct raw-wool business in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The application describes American Dutch Wools, its European affiliates, prewar Japanese sales through Iida and Company, and Ingster's intended commercial itinerary. Supporting sheets argue that direct representation in Japan is necessary for competitive wool purchasing and provide banking and trade references.

subfiles.title: Supplementary information on Joseph Ingster and American Dutch Wools
subfiles.about: Supplies Ingster's nationality and corporate ownership, banking, capitalization, and officer information.
subfiles.summary: Schwerdt identifies Ingster as a Polish-born Canadian and describes American Dutch Wools as a subsidiary of a Dutch firm.

subfiles.title: Clearance of Emilio Virata for Okinawa
subfiles.about: Records Virata's ten-day clearance for official travel to Okinawa and discussion of his documentation.
subfiles.summary: The Philippine Embassy was advised of the clearance but believed Virata might already have departed for Manila.

subfiles.title: Spanish request for Vicente Arnal's Japan permit
subfiles.about: Requests delivery of Vicente Arnal's travel permit upon his arrival in New York.
subfiles.summary: Spain reports that occupation authorities had agreed to permit its cultural attaché to return to Japan.

subfiles.title: Return of Emilio Virata's unused military permit
subfiles.about: Returns Virata's permit because his location was uncertain and he may already have departed.
subfiles.summary: State reports the Philippine Embassy would treat the case as closed if Virata had left for Manila.

subfiles.title: Return of Yusup Abubakar's unused military permit
subfiles.about: Returns Abubakar's permit because he departed before it could be used.
subfiles.summary: Abubakar sailed on December 27 and could not use his December 26 military permit.

subfiles.title: Yusup Abubakar's Yokohama transit clearance
subfiles.about: Records a ten-hour Japan clearance that Abubakar could not use because he had already sailed.
subfiles.summary: The permit covered a brief Yokohama call while Abubakar traveled to Manila aboard the President Cleveland.

subfiles.title: Document charge-out forms
subfiles.about: Blank forms for recording the circulation of documents and enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Two largely blank document-control sheets.

subfiles.title: Manila request for Marcelo Nubla's Japan entry
subfiles.about: Requests authorization for businessman Marcelo Nubla to enter Japan to inspect and collect surplus property.
subfiles.summary: The partially illegible cable proposes Nubla's early-February arrival at Yokohama by air.

subfiles.title: Approval of Marcelo Nubla's entry
subfiles.about: Reports military permission for Nubla to enter Japan between February 1 and April 1.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is instructed to document Nubla under SCAP Circular 8.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of directives on illegal Korean immigration
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Encloses SCAP directives concerning suppression of illegal Korean entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: The despatch transmits the 1947 amendment and the underlying 1946 directive.

subfiles.title: SCAP amendment on repatriated Korean illegal immigrants, copy one
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Japanese Government through the Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: Adds controls on baggage, registration cards, ration cards, and false papers held by repatriated Korean migrants.
subfiles.summary: The amendment limits baggage and directs officials to confiscate documents that could facilitate renewed illegal entry into Japan.

subfiles.title: SCAP amendment on repatriated Korean illegal immigrants, duplicate copy
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Japanese Government through the Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: Duplicates the directive adding document and baggage controls for Koreans returned south of the 38th parallel.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of the December 23 amendment intended to discourage repeated illegal immigration from Korea.

subfiles.title: SCAP directive suppressing illegal entry from Korea
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Imperial Japanese Government through the Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: Orders measures to detect illegal vessels and repatriate Korean migrants entering Japan.
subfiles.summary: The directive requires seizure of illegal ships, delivery of crews and passengers to designated ports, guarded transport to reception centers, and onward repatriation. Allied guards could support Japanese police when requested.

subfiles.title: Military permit for Marcelo Nubla
subfiles.about: Authorizes Marcelo Nubla to enter Japan at Yokohama for business.
subfiles.summary: Army permit issued against Nubla's passport, with Yokohama entry and business-purpose endorsements.

subfiles.title: Referral of Marcelo Nubla's application to SCAP
subfiles.about: Forwards Manila's request for Nubla to inspect and collect surplus Philippine property in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Military Permit Section is asked to seek SCAP's decision and notify Protective Services.

subfiles.title: Document charge-out forms
subfiles.about: Blank forms for tracking charged-out documents and enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Two largely blank file-control sheets.

subfiles.title: Manila request for Frank Lingenco's entry
subfiles.about: Requests consideration of Philippine businessman Frank Lingenco for entry to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The poorly reproduced telegram concerns Lingenco's proposal to sell liquor to occupation officers' clubs.

subfiles.title: Trader-quota processing for Manuel Sternberg
subfiles.about: Reports that Commerce will submit Sternberg for the February United States trader quota.
subfiles.summary: The February 1–15 quota is identified as Sternberg's earliest possible opportunity for SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: Unfavorable decision on Frank Lingenco
subfiles.about: Reports that military authorities were not favorably disposed toward Lingenco's proposed travel.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is notified of the adverse decision on Lingenco's application.

subfiles.title: Action slip denying Frank Lingenco's travel
subfiles.about: Marks Lingenco's proposed travel to Japan as not favorably considered.
subfiles.summary: Formal action slip recording denial of Lingenco's request.

subfiles.title: Referral of Frank Lingenco's application
subfiles.about: Forwards Lingenco's request to sell liquor to officers' clubs in Japan.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Army to submit Lingenco's application to SCAP and report the decision.

subfiles.title: Commerce processing of Manuel Sternberg
subfiles.about: Records Commerce's agreement to include Sternberg in the February trader quota.
subfiles.summary: Sternberg's firm was approved, but his British nationality still required SCAP authorization before travel.

subfiles.title: Clearance of Sherif Soubra and wife
subfiles.about: Records notification of Lebanon that the Soubras could enter Japan during January.
subfiles.summary: The Lebanese Legation agreed to prepare Circular 8 documentation; Mrs. Soubra would receive no occupation-force logistical support.

subfiles.title: Formal notification of the Soubras' clearance
subfiles.about: Confirms entry dates, documentation requirements, and denial of logistical support to Mrs. Soubra.
subfiles.summary: State formally confirms the Soubras' SCAP clearance and asks Lebanon to issue the statement required by Circular 8.

subfiles.title: Response concerning Koichitaro Suzuki's departure from Japan
subfiles.about: Addresses Brazil's request to let Suzuki leave Japan without the prescribed travel document.
subfiles.summary: State declines to seek an exception directly and suggests that Brazil authorize the Portuguese Legation in Tokyo, its protecting power, to issue Suzuki an identity certificate and approach military authorities.

subfiles.title: Military Permit Section memorandum
subfiles.from: Military Permit Section, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Transmits an almost entirely illegible communication concerning travel or permit processing.
subfiles.summary: Army memorandum whose substantive text is unreadable in the OCR.
